subject: DPA redline: enclave export carveout — product & security sign-off needed

Cc: mark.reynolds@biohealth.com

Subject: BioHealth DPA redline (enclave export carveout request)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our latest DPA redline (BioHealth_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) — the primary outstanding item for procurement is a narrowly scoped carveout that would allow BioHealth to pull aggregated embeddings and anonymized feature exports from a Redwood-managed customer enclave to our analytics stack for cohort analysis. We tried to capture the limits we need in the attached markup, but key asks are:

- Export type: aggregated embeddings (no raw PII) exported as encrypted tarball over a mutually authenticated TLS channel.
- Frequency: daily batch export (one file/day).
- Retention: 30 days on Redwood side before automatic deletion.
- Purpose: analytics & model telemetry only.
- Subprocessor note: export is to BioHealth Analytics (internal analytics team / AWS account).

Procurement needs confirmation that Product & Security are comfortable with the carveout language and the operational controls listed on pages 4–5. If we can get sign-off by end of week, we can move to executed DPA and a pilot shortly after.

Attachments: BioHealth_DPA_redline_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Sara Patel

On Thu, Aug 7, 2027 at 9:43 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dev / Olga — can you review the attached redline and the three bullets above?

Quick product read: the export pattern they describe is feasible but not currently a first-class flow in our runtime. Implementation options and tradeoffs:

A) Export job (recommended pilot): nightly job that snapshots aggregated embeddings from the enclave, writes an encrypted artifact to a transient S3 location, and pushes a signed manifest. Minimal runtime changes; we already have snapshot + KV tooling that can be adapted. Work estimate: 2 sprints to ship a safe pilot (engine + ops + QA).

B) API-based streaming export: real-time export would require more significant changes (auth, throttling, backpressure) — not recommended for initial scope.

Product caveats / questions for BioHealth:
- What exact schema do you need for the aggregated embedding file? (shape, serialization)
- Expected data volume (avg MB/file) and max training window (30 days ok?).
- Who will hold the KMS keys for the artifact at rest? (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed in their AWS account)

Risk/rollback: we need an abort/recall path if an export contains unexpected fields; propose a staged pilot with sample verification before automated daily exports.

I'll open a short-lived roadmap ticket and can prioritize a two-sprint pilot if legal/procurement needs the timeline.

—Dev
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BioHealth DPA redline (enclave export carveout request)

Thanks for the tag. Security review summary and conditional sign-off requirements below.

Summary: A daily export of aggregated embeddings can be acceptable provided strict controls are in place. My asks for contract language and operational evidence:

1) Scope & data minimization: contract must explicitly limit exported fields to aggregated embeddings only and prohibit any PII or raw transcripts.
2) Key management: prefer customer-managed KMS in their AWS account for final storage; if Redwood holds KMS, we require HSM-backed keys and separate key usage policies.
3) Attestation & audit: daily integrity manifests signed by client cert; Redwood must retain an immutable audit trail of export jobs and access (30 days minimum).
4) Subprocessor update: BioHealth must provide the target AWS account id and a named point of contact; add BioHealth analytics cluster to our allowed subprocessor list for this SLA.
5) Testing & pilot: require a verification window (3 days of manual sample checks) before enabling automated daily exports.

Controls we will require operationally (we will capture in the enclave appendix): encrypted in transit (mTLS), artifact signing, manifest verification, automated retention TTL, alerting for schema drift, and emergency recall process. See attached draft appendix for the technical controls we expect.

If Legal/Procurement can accept those conditions, Security is prepared to sign off. Olga — please confirm whether the appendix language is sufficient or if you want further tightening.

Attachments: redwood_enclave_appendix_draft.docx

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BioHealth DPA redline (enclave export carveout request) — summary & next steps

Sara / Mark — thank you for the redline and patience while we triaged internally. TL;DR: Redwood can accept a narrowly scoped enclave export carveout subject to the conditions below. If you agree, Procurement can proceed to countersign and we’ll begin a 2-week pilot timeline.

Agreed conditions (summary):
- Export: aggregated embeddings only; no PII or raw transcripts.
- Frequency: daily batch export (one encrypted artifact/day).
- Retention: Redwood retains artifacts and audit logs for 30 days; artifacts auto-delete after TTL.
- Keys: preference for customer-managed KMS in BioHealth AWS account; if Redwood manages keys, HSM-backed keys and split-access required.
- Pilot: 3-day manual verification window then automated daily exports.
- Subprocessor: BioHealth must provide target AWS account id; we will list that account as an allowed destination subprocessor in the DPA amendment.
- Controls: mTLS, artifact signing, manifest verification, alerting for schema drift, emergency recall process.

Next steps:
1) BioHealth to confirm the technical schema and provide target AWS account id (reply to this thread).
2) Procurement: if you accept the conditions above, we will send an enclave appendix + one-page controls addendum for signatures (DocuSign link below).
3) Product will schedule a pilot sprint (estimated 2 sprints to ship the pilot; ops/QA included).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=abc123-enclave-appendix
